```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2018_doripenem"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2018_doripenem"))$description`
* Article: [Ther Drug Monit 2018;40(4):425-433](https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000000528) (open access, PMC6075885)
* Supplement: Supplemental Digital Content 1 (<http://links.lww.com/TDM/A250>),
  individual demographics, NCA and post hoc PK parameters.

# Population

Twelve healthy Korean volunteers (6 men, 6 women) were enrolled at Pusan
National University Hospital; one man did not attend, so the analysis
holds 11 subjects (5 men, 6 women) with 12 plasma samples each (0, 0.33,
0.67, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 h after the start of the infusion).
Every subject received a single 250 mg doripenem dose infused over 1 hour.
Table 1 of the paper: age 22-30 years (median 24), weight 50-80 kg (median
57.0, mean 60.9, CV 16.6%), BMI 19-26 kg/m^2, serum creatinine 0.56-0.95
mg/dL and Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 101-139 mL/min (median 123).
Doripenem was measured by UHPLC-MS/MS (LLOQ 0.01 mg/L), and the model was
fitted in NONMEM 7.3 with FOCE-I.

The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2018_doripenem"))$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at 57 kg) | 22.0 L/h | Table 3, 'CL (L/h)' estimate |
| `lvc` (Vc at 57 kg) | 16.0 L | Table 3, 'VC (L)' estimate |
| `lq` (Q at 57 kg) | 1.83 L/h | Table 3, 'Q (L/h)' estimate |
| `lvp` (Vp at 57 kg) | 3.13 L | Table 3, 'VP (L)' estimate |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Results (allometric equation); Table 3 footnote |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Results (allometric equation); Table 3 footnote |
| Reference weight | 57 kg | Results, 'WTMED of 57 kg'; Table 1 median |
| `etalcl` variance | log(1 + 0.316^2) = 0.09518 | Table 3, 'omega CL (%)' = 31.6 |
| `etalvc` variance | log(1 + 0.353^2) = 0.11796 | Table 3, 'omega V (%)' = 35.3 |
| `etalcl`-`etalvc` covariance | 0.871 x sqrt(0.09518 x 0.11796) = 0.09218 | Table 3, 'omega CL-V correlation' = 0.871 |
| `propSd` | 0.301 | Table 3, 'sigma Proportional'; Results error equation Y = PRED + PRED x eps |
| Two-compartment IV structure | n/a | Results ('2-compartment model'; ADVAN3 in Methods) |
| No IIV on Q and Vp | n/a | Table 3 (IIV on CL and V only); Supplementary Table 3 Q and Vp vary only with weight |

# Structural checks against the paper's own numbers

## Closed-form two-compartment solution

The model is solved numerically. For the 57-kg typical subject, the
profile after a 250 mg 1-hour infusion must equal the closed-form
biexponential infusion solution built from the same CL, Vc, Q and Vp.

```{r closed-form}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2018_doripenem")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

t_grid <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 12, by = 0.25))
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 250, rate = 250, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = t_grid, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 57)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame",
                           rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
stopifnot("peripheral1" %in% names(sim_typ))

two_cmt_infusion <- function(t, dose, tinf, cl, vc, q, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc; k12 <- q / vc; k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  beta  <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  A <- (alpha - k21) / (vc * alpha * (alpha - beta))
  B <- (k21 - beta) / (vc * beta * (alpha - beta))
  r0 <- dose / tinf
  during <- function(tt) r0 * (A * (1 - exp(-alpha * tt)) + B * (1 - exp(-beta * tt)))
  ifelse(
    t <= tinf,
    during(t),
    r0 * (A * (1 - exp(-alpha * tinf)) * exp(-alpha * (t - tinf)) +
            B * (1 - exp(-beta * tinf)) * exp(-beta * (t - tinf)))
  )
}

cf <- two_cmt_infusion(sim_typ$time, 250, 1, 22.0, 16.0, 1.83, 3.13)
rel_err <- abs(sim_typ$Cc - cf) / pmax(cf, 1e-3)
max(rel_err[sim_typ$time > 0])
# Measured ~1e-8 at rtol 1e-10; a wrong structure (lost peripheral
# compartment, wrong volume) moves this by tens of percent.
stopifnot(max(rel_err[sim_typ$time > 0]) < 1e-5)
```

## Supplementary Table 3: individual post hoc parameters

Supplementary Table 3 lists each subject's post hoc CL, Vc, Q and Vp and
the derived half-lives. Q and Vp carry no IIV, so their individual values
must follow from body weight alone through the fixed allometric exponents
and the 57-kg reference. Plugging each subject's post hoc CL and Vc into
the packaged model (as the subject's own `lcl` / `lvc`) must also
reproduce the published t1/2 (ln 2 / K10) and t1/2beta.

```{r supp-table-3}
supp <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~WT, ~cl_pub, ~vc_pub, ~q_pub, ~vp_pub, ~thalf_pub, ~thalfb_pub,
  1L, 80, 18.9, 13.0, 2.36, 4.39, 0.479, 1.53,
  2L, 67, 16.9, 16.0, 2.07, 3.68, 0.655, 1.50,
  3L, 66, 17.4, 13.7, 2.04, 3.62, 0.546, 1.46,
  4L, 75, 24.5, 18.8, 2.25, 4.12, 0.532, 1.45,
  5L, 63, 27.5, 23.7, 1.97, 3.46, 0.598, 1.37,
  6L, 53, 37.1, 23.0, 1.73, 2.91, 0.429, 1.25,
  7L, 50, 18.7, 15.1, 1.66, 2.74, 0.559, 1.32,
  8L, 57, 22.6, 12.0, 1.83, 3.13, 0.368, 1.32,
  9L, 53, 32.9, 25.1, 1.73, 2.91, 0.530, 1.27,
  10L, 55, 23.9, 18.9, 1.78, 3.02, 0.549, 1.32,
  11L, 51, 20.2, 13.0, 1.68, 2.80, 0.446, 1.30
)

# Each subject's own CL and Vc enter as lcl / lvc at the subject's weight.
ind_par <- supp |>
  dplyr::transmute(id,
                   lcl = log(cl_pub / (WT / 57)^0.75),
                   lvc = log(vc_pub / (WT / 57)))

obs_times <- c(0, 0.33, 0.67, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8)
dense_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2.05, 24, by = 0.05))))
ev_ind <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  supp |> dplyr::transmute(id, WT, time = 0, amt = 250, rate = 250, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = supp$id, time = dense_times) |>
    dplyr::left_join(supp |> dplyr::select(id, WT), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(ind_par, by = "id")

sim_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_ind,
                           returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)

ind_chk <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl, vc, q, vp) |>
  dplyr::left_join(supp, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp, s = k10 + k12 + k21,
    beta = (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2,
    thalf_sim = log(2) / k10,
    thalfb_sim = log(2) / beta,
    q_pct = 100 * (q / q_pub - 1),
    vp_pct = 100 * (vp / vp_pub - 1),
    thalf_pct = 100 * (thalf_sim / thalf_pub - 1),
    thalfb_pct = 100 * (thalfb_sim / thalfb_pub - 1)
  )

ind_chk |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Subject = id, `WT (kg)` = WT,
    `Q model` = signif(q, 3), `Q paper` = q_pub,
    `Vp model` = signif(vp, 3), `Vp paper` = vp_pub,
    `t1/2 model` = signif(thalf_sim, 3), `t1/2 paper` = thalf_pub,
    `t1/2beta model` = signif(thalfb_sim, 3), `t1/2beta paper` = thalfb_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Individual parameters: packaged model vs Supplementary Table 3 of Kim 2018 (units L/h, L, h).")

# Deterministic: every difference is three-significant-figure rounding
# in the published table (largest about 0.3%). A wrong reference weight
# or exponent moves Q and Vp by several percent for the heavier subjects.
stopifnot(
  nrow(ind_chk) == 11L,
  max(abs(ind_chk$q_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(ind_chk$vp_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(ind_chk$thalf_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(ind_chk$thalfb_pct)) < 1.5
)
```

The individual profiles implied by these post hoc parameters can also be
compared with the subjects' observed noncompartmental results
(Supplementary Table 2). The post hoc AUCinf is Dose / CL by construction;
Cmax at the end of the infusion is where the paper itself reports the
model under-predicting (Figure 1 and Results: 'Most Cmax values were
slightly underpredicted').

```{r supp-table-2}
supp_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~cmax_obs, ~aucinf_obs,
  1L, 10.7, 14.0,
  2L, 10.3, 15.4,
  3L, 13.8, 16.3,
  4L, 7.70, 9.80,
  5L, 7.53, 9.81,
  6L, 7.03, 6.70,
  7L, 10.2, 14.5,
  8L, 13.0, 13.8,
  9L, 7.28, 7.08,
  10L, 8.44, 10.8,
  11L, 10.9, 14.1
)

conc_ind <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc)
dose_ind <- ev_ind |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt)

nca_ind <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ind, Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ind, amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))

ind_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_ind) |>
  dplyr::select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(supp_nca, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(supp |> dplyr::select(id, cl_pub), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_identity = aucinf.obs * cl_pub / 250)

# Deterministic identity: AUCinf x CL == Dose for each subject (PKNCA
# trapezoid on a 0.02-0.05 h grid out to 24 h; measured within 0.1%).
stopifnot(nrow(ind_nca) == 11L, max(abs(ind_nca$auc_identity - 1)) < 0.005)

ind_nca |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Subject = id,
    `Cmax post hoc` = signif(cmax, 3), `Cmax observed` = cmax_obs,
    `AUCinf post hoc` = signif(aucinf.obs, 3), `AUCinf observed` = aucinf_obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Post hoc individual predictions vs observed NCA (Supplementary Table 2); Cmax in mg/L, AUCinf in h*mg/L.")

ind_dev <- ind_nca |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax_median_pct = median(100 * (cmax / cmax_obs - 1)),
    auc_median_pct = median(100 * (aucinf.obs / aucinf_obs - 1))
  )
ind_dev
```

The post hoc Cmax sits below the observed Cmax for most subjects, as the
paper states, and the post hoc AUCinf is a few percent below the observed
NCA AUCinf. Both are properties of the published fit, not of the
transcription.

# Virtual cohort

Original observed data are not publicly available. The VPC and NCA
comparison below use 200 virtual subjects whose body weights are
resampled from the 11 individual weights of Supplementary Table 1, each
receiving the study dose (250 mg over 1 hour) and sampled at the study
times plus a denser grid for NCA.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20180528)
n_sub <- 200L
wt_obs <- supp$WT

vpc_times <- c(0, 0.33, 0.67, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8)
nca_times <- sort(unique(c(vpc_times, seq(0, 2, by = 0.1), seq(2.5, 12, by = 0.5))))

cohort <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_len(n_sub),
                         WT = sample(wt_obs, n_sub, replace = TRUE),
                         treatment = "250 mg 1-h infusion")

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 250, rate = 250, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = nca_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3: visual predictive check

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% vpc_times) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:8) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Doripenem concentration (mg/L)",
       title = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kim 2018 (250 mg single 1-h infusion, 200 virtual subjects).")
```

Read off Figure 3 of the paper, the 95th-percentile line peaks at about
17 mg/L at 1 hour, the median at about 7.5 mg/L and the 5th percentile at
about 2.5 mg/L. The simulated median at 1 hour reproduces the published
median; the simulated 5th-95th percentile band at 1 hour (roughly 3 to 15
mg/L) is somewhat narrower than the published one. The published band is
narrower than a residual SD of 0.549 (the variance reading of 0.301) would
give at its lower end, so the paper's VPC does not support either reading
exactly; see Assumptions and deviations for why 0.301 is taken as an SD.

```{r figure-3-check}
vpc_1h <- vpc |> dplyr::filter(time == 1)
vpc_1h
# Robust centre check: the median at the end of infusion is driven by Vc
# and the dose; a mis-scaled volume or dose moves it by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(vpc_1h$Q50 / 7.5 - 1) < 0.2)
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

# Every subject has a time-zero observation row from the event table.
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time == 0, sim_nca$id, any)))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 2 of Kim 2018 reports arithmetic means for the 11 subjects; the
simulated values below are arithmetic means over the 200 virtual subjects
so the two columns are like for like.

```{r nca_compare}
sim_means <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,            ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~cl.obs,
  "250 mg 1-h infusion",  9.72,  1,     12.0,        1.01,       22.7
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "h*mg/L",
            half.life = "h", cl.obs = "L/h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (mean of 200) vs published (Table 2 mean) NCA. * differs by more than 20%.")

pct <- function(code) {
  s <- sim_means$PPORRES[sim_means$PPTESTCD == code]
  r <- published[[code]]
  stopifnot(length(s) == 1L, length(r) == 1L)
  100 * (s / r - 1)
}
# Exposure and clearance: the mean of 200 subjects has a standard error of
# about 2.5% (CV of 1/CL about 33%), so 15% is several SE wide and still
# catches a mis-transcribed CL, dose or unit.
stopifnot(abs(pct("aucinf.obs")) < 15, abs(pct("cl.obs")) < 15)
```

* **AUCinf and CL** agree with Table 2 within about 10% (AUCinf about 5%
  low, CL about 10% high; the cohort mean of CL sits above the 57-kg
  typical value because of the weight scaling and the log-normal IIV).
* **Cmax** is lower than the observed mean. The paper itself reports that
  the model under-predicts most observed Cmax values (Results; Figures 1
  and 2), and the post hoc comparison above shows the same shortfall for
  the 11 real subjects. It is a property of the published fit.
* **Half-life** is longer than the NCA t1/2-lambda-z of 1.01 h. The
  simulated value reflects the model's terminal (beta) phase, whose post
  hoc mean in Supplementary Table 3 is 1.37 h; the paper's Discussion
  reports the NCA half-life as significantly different from t1/2beta
  (Wilcoxon P = 0.014) and attributes it to distribution-phase samples
  entering the lambda-z regression.

## Figure 4: probability of target attainment

The paper simulated 10,000 patients at steady state with weights drawn
from a log-normal distribution, an unbound fraction of 0.919, and the
target 40% fT>MIC. Patients were split at the first quartile of the
simulated beta half-life (1.3 h). The replication below uses 200 virtual
patients per regimen (weights log-normal with the cohort mean 60.9 kg and
CV 16.6%, Table 1) and individual predictions without residual error.
Because the model is linear, concentrations for 750 and 1000 mg are the
500 mg profile scaled by dose.

```{r figure-4-sim}
set.seed(4040)
n_pta <- 200L
sdlog_wt <- sqrt(log(1 + 0.166^2))
pta_cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_pta),
  WT = rlnorm(n_pta, log(60.9) - sdlog_wt^2 / 2, sdlog_wt)
)

regimens <- tidyr::expand_grid(tinf = c(1, 2, 3, 4), tau = c(8, 12)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reg = dplyr::row_number())

ev_pta <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  ids <- pta_cohort |> dplyr::mutate(id = id + (i - 1L) * n_pta, reg = r$reg)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    ids |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 500, rate = 500 / r$tinf, ii = r$tau,
                         ss = 1L, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
    tidyr::expand_grid(ids, time = seq(0, r$tau, by = 0.02)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0L, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  )
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

# One draw of individual parameters per virtual patient, reused across the
# eight regimens: the paper evaluated every regimen in the same patients.
omega_cl_vc <- matrix(c(0.09518, 0.09218, 0.09218, 0.11796), 2)
eta_draw <- matrix(rnorm(2 * n_pta), ncol = 2) %*% chol(omega_cl_vc)
eta_df <- tibble::tibble(id0 = seq_len(n_pta),
                         etalcl = eta_draw[, 1], etalvc = eta_draw[, 2])
pta_par <- tidyr::expand_grid(reg = regimens$reg, id0 = seq_len(n_pta)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(eta_df, by = "id0") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = id0 + (reg - 1L) * n_pta,
                lcl = log(22.0) + etalcl, lvc = log(16.0) + etalvc) |>
  dplyr::select(id, lcl, lvc)
# Individual lcl / lvc ride on the event table: a data column named like a
# parameter overrides that parameter for the subject.
ev_pta <- dplyr::left_join(ev_pta, pta_par, by = "id")
stopifnot(!anyNA(ev_pta$lcl))

sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_pta, keep = "reg",
                           returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6,
                           ssRtol = 1e-8, ssAtol = 1e-10)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
fu <- 0.919
mics <- c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)

beta_t <- sim_pta |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0, reg == 1) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp, s = k10 + k12 + k21,
                beta = (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2,
                thalfb = log(2) / beta) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id0 = id, thalfb)
quantile(beta_t$thalfb, c(0.25, 0.5))
# The paper's split point (first quartile of the simulated beta half-life,
# 1.3 h) is set by the CL-Vc IIV block. With 200 patients the standard
# error of the first quartile is about 0.01 h; an omega read on the wrong
# scale moves it by more than 0.1 h.
stopifnot(abs(quantile(beta_t$thalfb, 0.25) - 1.3) < 0.06)

ft <- sim_pta |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id0 = (id - 1L) %% n_pta + 1L) |>
  dplyr::left_join(regimens, by = "reg") |>
  dplyr::filter(time < tau)

pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(500, 750, 1000), mic = mics) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(res = list(
    ft |>
      dplyr::group_by(reg, tinf, tau, id0) |>
      dplyr::summarise(ftmic = mean(fu * Cc * dose / 500 > mic), .groups = "drop")
  )) |>
  tidyr::unnest(res) |>
  dplyr::left_join(beta_t, by = "id0") |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = ifelse(thalfb < 1.3, "beta half-life < 1.3", "beta half-life > 1.3")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, mic, tinf, tau, group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PTA = 100 * mean(ftmic >= 0.4), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pta, aes(factor(mic), PTA, group = factor(tinf), shape = factor(tinf))) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(paste(dose, "mg") ~ group + paste0("Interval: ", tau, " h")) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Probability of target attainment (%)",
       shape = "Infusion time (h)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Kim 2018 (40% fT>MIC, fu = 0.919).") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

The paper's dosing conclusions, checked against the replication (PTA in
percent; the paper's criterion is PTA >= 90%):

```{r figure-4-claims}
cell <- function(dose_, tinf_, tau_, mic_, grp) {
  v <- pta$PTA[pta$dose == dose_ & pta$tinf == tinf_ & pta$tau == tau_ &
                 pta$mic == mic_ & pta$group == grp]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique PTA cell")
  v
}
lo <- "beta half-life < 1.3"; hi <- "beta half-life > 1.3"
claims <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Claim, ~Value,
  "500 mg 1-h q8h, MIC 0.5, t1/2beta > 1.3 h: optimal (>= 90%)", cell(500, 1, 8, 0.5, hi),
  "500 mg 1-h q8h, MIC 0.5, t1/2beta < 1.3 h: not sufficient", cell(500, 1, 8, 0.5, lo),
  "500 mg 2-h q8h, MIC 1, t1/2beta > 1.3 h: appropriate", cell(500, 2, 8, 1, hi),
  "500 mg 3-h q8h, MIC 1, t1/2beta < 1.3 h: appropriate", cell(500, 3, 8, 1, lo),
  "500 mg 4-h q8h, MIC 2, both groups: appropriate (lower group)", min(cell(500, 4, 8, 2, lo), cell(500, 4, 8, 2, hi)),
  "750 mg 3-h q8h, MIC 2, both groups: appropriate (lower group)", min(cell(750, 3, 8, 2, lo), cell(750, 3, 8, 2, hi)),
  "1000 mg 4-h q8h, MIC 4, both groups: required (lower group)", min(cell(1000, 4, 8, 4, lo), cell(1000, 4, 8, 4, hi))
)
knitr::kable(claims, digits = 0, caption = "Dosing statements from Kim 2018 Results vs simulated PTA (%).")
```

With 200 patients per regimen (about 50 in the short half-life group)
each PTA cell carries a binomial standard error of several percent, so
cells that sit near 90% in the paper's Figure 4 can fall either side of
the line; the table is reported rather than asserted.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error scale.** Table 3 gives 'sigma Proportional' = 0.301,
  and the Results text calls the residual variance omega^2. The value is
  taken as the proportional SD (30.1%). Digitised by the maintainers from
  Figure 2D, the observed-to-individual-prediction scatter has a relative
  spread of about 0.29-0.32, consistent with an SD of 0.301 and not with an
  SD of 0.549 (the variance reading). The published VPC (Figure 3) has an
  upper band closer to the variance reading and a lower band closer to the
  SD reading, so it does not discriminate.
* **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports IIV as CV%. The variances use
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (0.0952 and 0.1180); reading CV as sqrt(omega^2)
  would give 0.0999 and 0.1246, a difference that does not change any
  result above. The simulated first quartile of the beta half-life
  (about 1.3 h) matches the value the paper used to split its Monte Carlo
  cohort.
* **No IIV on Q and Vp.** Table 3 lists IIV on CL and V only, and the
  individual Q and Vp in Supplementary Table 3 vary only with body weight,
  which the model reproduces to rounding.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Age, sex, Cockcroft-Gault
  creatinine clearance and serum creatinine were tested and not retained;
  they are documented in `covariatesDataExcluded`. Body weight enters only
  through the a priori allometric scaling.
* **Table 2 Clast.** Table 2 prints a mean Clast of 49.0 mg/L (range
  12.0-111), which cannot be in mg/L given a Cmax near 10 mg/L; the
  individual Clast values in Supplementary Table 2 (0.012-0.189 mg/L)
  indicate the Table 2 entries are in ng/mL. Clast is not used here.
* **PTA simulation details.** The paper does not give the weight
  distribution parameters, whether residual error entered the fT>MIC
  calculation, or the random seed. The replication uses the Table 1 mean
  and CV of weight, individual predictions without residual error, and
  200 rather than 10,000 patients per regimen.
* **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-25.
